outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the challenge of mathematical reasoning for LLMs, the current landscape of open-source vs. proprietary models, and the primary goals of the DeepSeekMath project.
subtopics: Challenges of mathematical reasoning: Structure and complexity
Overview of benchmarks: MATH, GSM8K, CMATH, and Gaokao-Math
The gap between open-source and proprietary models (GPT-4, Gemini-Ultra)
Project Objectives: Scaling math pre-training and advancing RL techniques

outline.chapter_title: Scaling Mathematical Pre-training: Data Engineering at Scale
outline.description: This chapter details the systematic construction of the DeepSeekMath Corpus, focusing on data selection pipelines and quality validation.
subtopics: The Data Selection Pipeline: Using fastText classifiers for web data mining
Iterative Corpus Construction: Seed data, expansion, and human annotation
Data Decontamination: Filtering out benchmark questions to ensure integrity
Corpus Comparison: Analyzing DeepSeekMath vs. MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2
Multilingualism in Math Data: Impact on English and Chinese benchmarks

outline.description: This chapter covers the actual pre-training process of DeepSeekMath-Base and provides deep dives into the effects of code and academic data.
subtopics: Initialization Strategy: Why DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 is an ideal starting point
Training Recipe: Mixture of math, code, and natural language data
The Code Training Hypothesis: How code training enhances mathematical reasoning
The ArXiv Paradox: Analyzing why arXiv papers may not provide the expected boost
Generalization: Impact of math training on MMLU and BBH benchmarks

outline.description: This chapter explains how to transform a base model into an instruction-following model capable of step-by-step reasoning.
subtopics: SFT Data Curation: Combining CoT, PoT, and tool-integrated reasoning
Instruction Tuning Techniques: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) vs. Program-of-Thought (PoT)
Tool-Integrated Reasoning: Enabling models to use Python and external libraries
Evaluating DeepSeekMath-Instruct: Performance against proprietary and open-source models

outline.description: A core technical chapter introducing the GRPO algorithm as an efficient alternative to standard PPO for reinforcement learning.
subtopics: The Limitations of PPO: Memory and computational burdens of the critic model
GRPO Mechanics: Estimating baselines from group scores
Advantage Estimation: Relative rewards within a sampled group
Outcome Supervision (OS) vs. Process Supervision (PS): Fine-grained reward signals
Iterative RL: Continual reward model training and replay mechanisms

outline.chapter_title: A Unified Paradigm for Preference Optimization
outline.description: This chapter provides a theoretical framework to understand various alignment techniques like DPO, RFT, and PPO through a single mathematical lens.
subtopics: The Unified Objective Function: Data Source, Reward Function, and Algorithm
Online vs. Offline Sampling: Comparing RFT/DPO with Online RFT/GRPO
Gradient Coefficients: How different algorithms penalize or reinforce outputs
Empirical Analysis: Why RL works (Top-K robustness vs. fundamental capability)
Future Directions: Weak-to-Strong alignment, reward uncertainty, and advanced sampling

outline.description: The final chapter summarizes the findings, discusses the limitations of the current approach, and outlines future research directions.
subtopics: Summary of Achievements: Surpassing open-source state-of-the-art
Current Limitations: Geometry reasoning and few-shot capabilities
Data Selection Bias: Identifying gaps in pre-training content
Future Work: Improving data pipelines and robust RL against noisy rewards
